summary.text: Kayse Jama is a Democratic and Working Families Party state senator from Oregon Senate District 24 who was appointed in January 2021, became Senate majority leader ahead of the 2025 session, and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026.

paragraphs.text: Kayse Jama was born in Somalia and emigrated to the United States in 1998 as a refugee, settling in Portland.
He earned a B.A. in sociology from Marylhurst University, and his career includes work as a nonprofit executive director, policy advisor and community organizer.
Jama co-founded the Center for Intercultural Organizing, now Unite Oregon.
Jama ran for the Senate seat in 2018 and finished third in the Democratic primary behind Shemia Fagan and incumbent Rod Monroe.

Commissioners from Multnomah and Clackamas counties appointed him to the Senate in January 2021 to replace Fagan, who had been elected Oregon Secretary of State, and he was re-elected in 2022 with 59% of the vote.
He chaired the Housing and Development Committee in the 2021-2022 and 2023-2024 sessions, and was selected as Senate majority leader ahead of the 2025 session, replacing Kathleen Taylor.
